name: Brick works productivity vs rework cost (Palestine)
citation: Mahamid, I. (2020). Study of relationship between rework and labor productivity in building construction projects. Pontificia Universidad Catolica de Chile, Escuela de Construccion Civil (journal name to be confirmed from the PDF masthead)

variables.name: rework_cost_pct
variables.description: Rework cost in brick works as a percentage; the sample mean reported is 4.51%. Range of the data not extracted.

activity: Brick works in building construction (2-labour crew)
validity_text: Fitted on 40 building projects in Palestine; predictor range not extracted. Equation printed as Y = 34.36 - 1.71X (Equation 5 in the text, although the text also refers to Equation (3)); R2 = 0.78, F(1,39) = 62.71. Sample mean productivity 26.2 m2/day and mean rework 4.51%.
limitations: Single-variable model; Palestinian conditions; not Indian data; unknown range; crew of 2 labourers.

name: Block-laying productivity per block layer (Kampala, Uganda)
citation: Ouga, A.D., Alinaitwe, H.M., Mwesige, G. (2020). Modelling Block Laying Productivity on Building Sites in Kampala. Journal of Construction in Developing Countries, 25(1), 109-128. DOI: 10.21315/jcdc2020.25.1.6

variables.name: work_height_m
variables.description: Height above ground at which the wall is being built.

variables.name: porters_per_layer
variables.description: Number of porters (material carriers) supporting one block layer; NOT part of the crew-size scaling (already an input to this equation).

variables.name: exed
variables.description: 1 if the block layer has >= 5 years experience AND a craft/diploma qualification, else 0.

activity: Solid concrete block laying, block 400 x 225 x 200 mm, individual block layer with porters
validity_text: Kampala building sites; work height 0.5-5.5 m; porters observed 1-4 (44 of 70 observations at 2 porters).
limitations: Concrete block, not clay brick; Uganda, not India; per-block-layer hourly rate, not a crew-day rate; R2 0.65 leaves 35% unexplained; EX and ED individually not significant; text is inconsistent on n (70/83/160) and on the block size used in model development.
usage_note: output_basis=per_worker scales by workers_per_crew, but here 'worker' means block layers (masons) only: porters are already a model INPUT (porters_per_layer), not part of the crew multiplier. Set workers_per_crew to the number of masons/block-layers, and porters_per_layer to porters PER MASON, or this double-counts porter effort.
